tags: why do dogs wag their tail
script: Most people think a wagging tail always means a happy dog. That's actually one of the biggest myths in dog behavior. Tail wagging is really just a sign of emotional arousal, and that emotion could be happiness, but it could just as easily be nervousness, frustration, or even aggression. What actually matters is the position, speed, and direction of the wag. A tail held high and wagging stiffly and fast usually signals alertness or a warning, not friendliness. A tail wagging low and loose, almost like the whole back half of the body is wiggling, that's your genuinely relaxed, happy dog. Speed matters too. A slow wag can mean uncertainty, while a broad, fast sweep usually means excitement. There's even research showing dogs wag more to the right when they feel positive emotions, and more to the left when they feel negative ones, something other dogs can actually detect. So next time you see a wagging tail, don't just smile and assume everything's fine. Look at the whole picture, the ears, the posture, the pace of the wag, and you'll get a much more accurate read on what your dog is really feeling.
